---
title: "Overview"
---

This site documents the code for the paper *An atmospheric dryness threshold limits daytime net CO~2~ uptake in
forests* by Lukas Hörtnagl and coauthors, submitted to Nature Communications. The
analysis outputs and a snapshot of the code are deposited in the ETH Research
Collection: <https://doi.org/10.3929/ethz-c-000798579>.

The code analyzes the effects of vapor pressure deficit (VPD) and soil water content (SWC)
on daytime net ecosystem production (NEP) at 208 forest eddy covariance sites.

Each site has its own XGBoost model. The models are interpreted with out-of-sample SHAP
values from 5-fold cross-validation and with ALE curves. Site results are aggregated with
equal weight per site, overall and per IGBP forest type.

- Target: `NEP_ZSCORE`, half-hourly, daytime, four months of highest GPP per site.
  `GPP_ZSCORE`, `RECO_ZSCORE` and `ET_ZSCORE` run through the same pipeline as
  supporting analyses.
- Predictors: `TA_ZSCORE`, `SWIN_ZSCORE`, `VPD_ZSCORE`, `SWC_ZSCORE`.
- All variables are z-scored within site.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `scripts/10_datasets/` | Find and merge source datasets, check variable coverage, add ERA5 climate normals |
| `scripts/20_subsets/` | Build the per-site analysis subset and compute z-scores |
| `scripts/30_shap/` | Fit XGBoost models, compute SHAP values and ALE curves |
| `scripts/40_aggregation/` | Aggregate SHAP values per site, across sites, by forest type and by stress stage |
| `scripts/50_figures/` | Manuscript figures, tables and data files, each script named after the items it produces |
| `scripts/80_info/` | Checks quoted in the text or used in supplementary tables |
| `scripts/90_deposit/` | Source Data, demo data, deposit archives, the data flow chart, and the figure copies and column reference for this site |
| `src/` | Shared code: models, aggregation, plotting, statistics, curve fitting, stress stages, file handling, paths |
| `config/` | `settings.yaml`, FLUXNET and AmeriFlux site metadata, and the site climate tables read by script 17 |
| `data/worldmap/` | Natural Earth country outlines for the site map |

Source data and analysis outputs are not in the repository (see [Data](data.qmd)).

## Reading order

Start with [Installation](installation.qmd), then [Data](data.qmd), which shows how to
point the code at a data folder. [Pipeline](pipeline.qmd) lists the scripts in run order.
[Methods](methods.qmd) documents the choices that are hard to read from the code.
[Figures](figures.qmd) maps each display item to its script and shows the figures.
[Output columns](columns.qmd) describes every column of the deposited csv and parquet files.

## How to cite

Cite the code as:

Hörtnagl, L. (2026). ms-forests-vpd: analysis code for atmospheric dryness and forest net
CO~2~ uptake (version v2-revised). <https://github.com/holukas/ms-forests-vpd>

The data and code deposit is in the ETH Research Collection:
<https://doi.org/10.3929/ethz-c-000798579>.
[`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/holukas/ms-forests-vpd/blob/main/CITATION.cff) in the
repository holds the same reference, and GitHub shows it under "Cite this repository". The
paper reference will be added when the paper is published.
